name: New York
estimates: Presidential returns are from the tonmcg/US_County_Level_Election_Results_08-24 compilation (scraped from media result pages: Townhall 2016, Fox/Politico/NYT 2020, Fox 2024). They are close to but not the certified canvass; 2016 in particular is an election-week count and undercounts late-tallied ballots. "other" = total - dem - rep.
1 incorporated place(s) dropped: no ACS population row, or population 0.
1 place(s) whose internal point is outside every county polygon were assigned to the nearest county internal point.
5 place(s) have at least one null demographic (income/age/bach suppressed in ACS for small populations).
For places spanning several counties, "county" is the county containing the Gazetteer internal point. Place pop for consolidated city-counties is the "(balance)" figure where Census publishes one.

senate: 1 seat(s) have inc null (vacant in OpenStates or unmatched); they were placed on the district shapes holding the fewest seats, which for multi-member chambers is an approximation of where the vacancy really is.

District shapes are Census 2025 cartographic boundary files (SLDL/SLDU, 1:500k), i.e. the districts Census held as of that vintage; inc is the office-holder in the OpenStates "current" export on the build date, name and party only. District lat/lon is the centroid of the largest polygon of the simplified shape.

Demographics: ACS 2020-2024 5-year estimates (sample survey, subject to margin of error). white/black/asian are non-Hispanic single-race shares; hisp is Hispanic of any race. Income is top-coded by Census at 250,001.

Geometry simplified with mapshaper (interval 210 m, topology-preserving per layer; tiny islands dropped), coordinates rounded to 4 decimals. County, house and senate layers are simplified separately, so their borders can differ by up to the tolerance.
